column10: A mountain is a very tall natural landform that rises high above the land around it. They are found all over the world and often have rocky sides, plants, or snowy tops, with the very top called a peak. Mountains form over billions of years when huge pieces of the Earth called tectonic plates slowly pushed together. This causes the rock to crumple and push upward, like paper. Mountains can also form when volcanoes built up layers of rock. No person made them—they come from natural forces deep inside the planet. Mountains are special because they are some of the highest places on Earth, can be very cold at the top, and help create rivers and weather, and even though they can look different—some sharp, some round. There isn't exactly a 'first,' mountain, but the oldest mountains on the earth are the Makhonhwa Mountains, which are over three billion years old.
